title: Polar adaptations fact cards
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Living things and their habitats (Frozen Kingdom)
source: Seeded from science/y6 lesson 15 (Polar adaptations fact cards (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 15: Polar adaptations: blubber, fur and camouflage. To understand how polar animals are adapted to survive the cold

questions.q: How does white fur help a polar bear?
questions.a: Camouflage on snow, so it can sneak up on seals.
questions.model: Habitat: white snow and ice. Feature: white fur. Link: it blends in. So it helps the bear hunt without being seen.

questions.a: A thick layer of fat under the skin.
To share warmth and lose less heat.

questions.q: Core: Choose two polar animals. Make a fact file with three adaptations each and how each helps.
questions.a: For example: polar bear: white fur (camouflage), thick fur (warmth), wide paws (walk on snow).
questions.model: Teacher writes the first: walrus: blubber (keeps warm in icy water).

questions.q: Extend: Explain how camouflage helps an Arctic hare.
questions.a: It turns white in winter so predators find it harder to see.

questions.q: Stretch: Which human clothing copies polar adaptations? Explain one.
questions.a: For example: a padded coat traps air like fur; a wetsuit insulates like blubber.

questions.q: Big question: how do animals stay warm colder than a freezer?
questions.a: Blubber, thick fur or feathers trap heat, and huddling shares warmth.
